Here's a regex that matches an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```

- `\d{4}` matches the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.
- `\b` word boundaries keep it from matching inside longer digit strings.

It matches `2026-10-01`. It doesn't check that a day exists in its month, so `2026-02-31` also matches. Leap years and month lengths need a date parser rather than a regex.

For a whole-string match, such as validating input, use anchors instead of `\b`:

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```
